title: Cognitive Load Cliff: 10x Density Spike Between Foundations and Modern LLM Systems
structural_flaw: The curriculum allocates 7 full days to basic Python syntax (Week 1), but packs the entirety of modern LLM engineering (LoRA, QLoRA, 4-bit Quantization, GGUF, AWQ, Scaling Laws, Prompting) into a single 7-day sprint (Week 12).
evidence_analysis: Week 1 Concept Density: 49 basic syntax items over 7 days vs Week 12: 49 advanced frontier LLM architecture items in the same timeframe.
architectural_recommendation: Split Week 12 into a 2-week track: 'Week 12: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (LoRA/QLoRA/PEFT)' and 'Week 13: High-Performance Model Quantization (GGUF/AWQ/GPTQ)'.

title: Distributed Training & Parallelism Compression Bottleneck
structural_flaw: Week 21 attempts to teach DataParallel, DDP, Tensor Parallelism (Megatron-LM), Pipeline Parallelism (1F1B), FSDP, and DeepSpeed ZeRO-1/2/3 in 7 days, giving students <24 hours per distributed paradigm.
evidence_analysis: Week 21 covers 6 distinct cluster communication topologies and distributed memory models in 7 days.
architectural_recommendation: Introduce prerequisite inter-GPU communication primitives (NCCL, Ring-AllReduce, Broadcast) earlier in Week 8/17 before tackling multi-dimensional parallelism.

title: Mixture of Experts (MoE) Architecture Gaps
structural_flaw: DeepSeek, Mixtral, and modern frontier LLMs rely entirely on Sparse Mixture of Experts (MoE) with top-k gating, router load balancing, and expert capacity factors. The curriculum lacks a dedicated day on MoE routing.
evidence_analysis: Keyword 'moe' frequency across all 26 weeks: 0 mentions.
architectural_recommendation: Include a dedicated standalone Day in Week 12/19: 'Mixture of Experts (MoE) — Top-K Routing, Expert Parallelism & Load Balancing Loss'.

title: ColBERT & Late-Interaction Retrieval in Modern RAG
structural_flaw: Dense single-vector embeddings suffer from information loss on complex queries. Late-interaction token-level similarity (ColBERT / PLAID) is missing from Week 14/15 RAG modules.
evidence_analysis: Keyword 'colbert' frequency across all 26 weeks: 1 mentions.
architectural_recommendation: Add Multi-Vector & Late-Interaction Retrieval to Week 15 showing MaxSim operator computation.

title: Test-Time Compute & MCTS Reasoning Models (o1 / DeepSeek-R1)
structural_flaw: The shift from pretraining scaling to test-time search scaling (Monte Carlo Tree Search, Process Reward Models, Chain-of-Thought verification) is absent from Week 22 RLHF.
evidence_analysis: Keyword 'mcts' frequency across all 26 weeks: 0 mentions.
architectural_recommendation: Add a dedicated module on Test-Time Compute Scaling, Process Supervision (PRMs), and Monte Carlo Tree Search for LLM reasoning.

title: Multi-GPU & Cloud Infrastructure Execution Barrier on Student Laptops
structural_flaw: Weeks 18 (Kubernetes GPU clusters), 19 (TensorRT-LLM/Triton), and 21 (Multi-GPU DDP / DeepSpeed ZeRO-3) assign tasks requiring high-end multi-GPU clusters ($10k+ hardware) without providing local CPU fallback mocks or Google Colab / Kaggle cloud notebook execution bridges.
evidence_analysis: Tasks in Weeks 18 and 21 fail immediately on standard developer laptops (MacBooks, single-GPU PCs) without fallback simulators.
architectural_recommendation: Provide dual execution tracks: (1) Local PyTorch CPU/MPS multi-process simulation and (2) Zero-setup Google Colab T4/A100 launcher links for all GPU-intensive tasks.

title: LocalStorage Schema Fragility & Lack of State Migration Engine
structural_flaw: Student progress (XP, completed days, streak, quiz answers) is stored as unversioned raw keys in browser LocalStorage. A change to course structure or day numbering risks breaking student state without an automated migration handler.
evidence_analysis: No schema version key (e.g. `COURSE_SCHEMA_VERSION = '2.1'`) or migration function exists in `course.js`.
architectural_recommendation: Implement an atomic schema migration layer in `course.js` that checks schema version on boot and safely transforms legacy progress keys.

title: Lack of Offline Progressive Web App (PWA) Capability for 191-Day Roadmap
structural_flaw: As an intensive 6-month curriculum, students study in offline environments (transit, airplanes, low-connectivity zones). The web application lacks a Service Worker, Web Manifest, and cache manifest, preventing offline review.
evidence_analysis: No `sw.js` (Service Worker) or `manifest.json` found in root directory.
architectural_recommendation: Add a lightweight PWA Service Worker caching core CSS, JS, fonts, and HTML week pages for offline learning.

title: Code Sandbox 'Run' Button Fragility on CDN Failover
structural_flaw: The interactive 'Run' buttons in code blocks depend on external CDN scripts. If a student is behind a corporate firewall or offline, clicking 'Run' fails silently without showing an informative error or fallback output.
evidence_analysis: No CDN failover timeout or visual error state when code execution runtime is unreachable.
architectural_recommendation: Implement a 3-second runtime health-check with an inline message: 'Interactive runner offline. Code is display-ready for local terminal execution.'
